full_judgment:
2. Though the respondent appeared and filed written statements denying the charges, but ultimately did not contest the suit. Petitioner examined herself as P. W. 1 and examined her maternal Aunt Sandliya Rekha Goswami as P.W. 2. Being satisfied with the case of the petitioner the District Court passed decree on 10.2.1998 awarding the dissolution of the marriage. District Court, thereafter, forwarded the suit record to the High Court Division for confirmation of the decree as required under section 17 of the Divorce Act. The record is now registered as Divorce Suit No. 1 of 1998 of the High Court Division. 

 5. Considering the unchallenged testimony of the petitioner before the District Court and the additional evidence before us equally unchallenged, we find that the District Court is justified in dissolving the marriage and awarding the decree in the said suit. 

 7. We must express our regrets and sympathy to Eva for the inordinate delay in awarding the decree finally though there were justiciable grounds for it. Eva presented her petition before the District Court on 2.1.93 when she was 24 years. District Court passed the decree in her favour five years thereafter and it took about three years to confirm the decree. By now Eva is 30 years losing the five years of her youth, the prime part of the lift God bestows on a person. 

 that the decree dated 10.2.93 passed by the District Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 2 of 1993 dissolving the marriage between Eva Sunanda Chowdhury and Subir Sarker be and is confirmed. There will be no order as to costs.
